title: Chicano Style: Cultural History, Clothing and Women's Outfits
description: Explore Chicano fashion through Mexican-American history, structured volume and workwear, with five contemporary outfit interpretations.
primary_intent: Mexican-American/Chicano cultural history and structured workwear proportions; not generic Streetwear or a costume/stereotype checklist.

title: What Is Hippie Style? Counterculture and Fashion
description: Understand late-1960s and early-1970s hippie fashion through flow, craft and reuse, with six outfits and distinctions from Boho Chic.
primary_intent: Hippie counterculture, anti-fashion, craft and reuse; distinct from polished Boho Chic, broad Vintage and rural-romantic Cottagecore.

title: What Was Dior's New Look? The Silhouette That Changed Fashion in 1947
description: Explore Dior's 1947 New Look, the Bar suit's construction and postwar controversy, with contemporary interpretations of its proportions.
primary_intent: Dior 1947 debut and Bar construction/controversy; separate from complete 1950s overview, corset-item styling and broad Vintage.

title: What Is Ulzzang Style? Korean Fashion and Women's Outfits
description: Separate ulzzang's Korean internet origins from its later casual-fashion label, with six outfit formulas and no body or skin-color requirements.
primary_intent: Korean internet image/beauty origins and later international clothing label; not all K-fashion, Acubi layers, Clean Girl polish or body eligibility.

title: 1950s Women's Fashion: Silhouettes and Outfit Ideas
description: Explore full skirts, sheaths, suits, sportswear and later 1950s shapes, with six contemporary outfits beyond a single New Look silhouette.
primary_intent: Complete 1950s womenswear range and evolving occasion-based shapes; broader than Dior 1947 New Look and distinct from timeless Classic or generic Vintage.

title: Japanese Streetwear: Silhouettes, Layers and Women's Outfits
description: Build Japanese streetwear-inspired outfits through silhouette, layered lengths, vintage and considered selection, with six adaptable combinations.
primary_intent: Japan-context urban streetwear, Ura-Hara selection and layering; distinguish global Streetwear and Harajuku ecosystem including non-streetwear subcultures.

title: 1930s Fashion: Silhouettes, Clothing and Contemporary References
description: Understand natural waists, bias-cut gowns, daytime tailoring and Hollywood references, with six ways to interpret 1930s proportions today.
primary_intent: 1930s natural-waist elongated bias drape and changing shoulders; not 1920s flapper, postwar New Look full skirts or generic Vintage.
